listen_addresses.description: IP addresses and ports on which the MTA listens for inbound SMTP connections (relay mode only).

domain.description: Domain for which this route applies (wildcards allowed, e.g., `*.example.com`).

port.description: Port to use when connecting to the next hop MTA (25, 587, 465, etc.).

next_hop.description: Hostname or IP address of the upstream relay to which mail for this domain should be forwarded.

routes.description: List of routing rules defining how mail for specific domains should be relayed. Each rule maps a domain to an upstream relay.

tls_enabled.description: Enable TLS encryption for outbound connections to upstream relays. Requires valid certificates.

tls_cert_chain.description: Path to the certificate chain file (PEM format) for client-side TLS authentication (if upstream requires it).

tls_key.description: Path to the private key file (PEM format) matching the certificate chain.

tls_ca_file.description: Path to a bundle of trusted CA certificates (PEM format) for verifying upstream servers.

starttls_enabled.description: Whether to attempt STARTTLS negotiation with upstream relays when available (recommended for privacy).

connect_timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait for connection to upstream relay (TCP connect phase).

data_timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait for data transfer (SMTP DATA phase) with upstream relay.

session_timeout.description: Maximum idle time (seconds) for an SMTP session before closing it.

retry_max.description: Maximum number of retry attempts for a given message before giving up and bouncing.

retry_interval.description: Initial delay (seconds) before first retry of a failed delivery attempt.

retry_backoff.description: Multiplier for exponential backoff (retry delay grows as `interval * backoff^(attempt-1)`).

verbosity.description: Logging verbosity: 0 = minimal (errors only), 1 = normal (recommended), 2 = verbose, 3 = debug.

local_hostname.description: Override for the local hostname announced in SMTP HELO/EHLO (e.g., `mail.example.com`). If empty, system FQDN is used.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against the envelope sender address (e.g., `^user@localhost$`).

replacement.description: Replacement string (may use capture groups, e.g., `user@example.com`).

sender_maps.description: Rules to rewrite (masquerade) sender addresses in the envelope (e.g., to hide internal addresses).

bounce_sender.description: Envelope sender address to use for bounce messages (e.g., `mailer-daemon@example.com`). Empty means default system bounce address.
